article_claim: LFM2.5-1.2B has 10 attention layers and 6 ShortConv layers.
finding: The model card and config.json list 16 layers: 10 convolution blocks and 6 GQA blocks.
impact: Kernel priority and state-memory estimates use the wrong layer ratio.

article_claim: TTFT 47 ms with TPOT 4 ms is about 42 ERS.
finding: The quoted formula gives 63.1851 ERS for that pair.
impact: Score targets and attribution cannot be trusted until evaluator units and aggregation are confirmed.

article_claim: The H200 MIG 1g.18gb slice has 1/7 of the SMs and 1/8 of the memory.
finding: NVIDIA's MIG profile table lists 1g.18gb with 1/7 compute and 1/8 memory.
impact: Full-H200 and other-architecture benchmarks are not faithful proxies.

article_claim: Speculative decoding with an LFM draft failed only because of ShortConv state rollback.
finding: A separate hybrid draft model also needs multiple KV-cache groups, while the vLLM drafter assumes one group/AttentionMetadata.
impact: Speculative decoding is a structural engineering project, not a flag-only experiment.

article_claim: Speculative decoding needs at least 90% acceptance to improve performance.
finding: No universal threshold was found; break-even depends on draft cost, verification cost, batch size and speculation length.
impact: Use measured accepted tokens per target invocation instead of an acceptance percentage.

article_claim: Real GPU compute per decode step is 0.017 ms (2.4 GFLOP / 141 TFLOP/s).
finding: The arithmetic holds, but FLOP divided by peak FLOP/s is a roofline lower bound, not measured compute time.
impact: It is not proof that compute optimization is useless; measure kernel durations.

article_claim: Each decode step loads about 0.6 GB of FP8 weights.
finding: vLLM online FP8 quantizes only Linear layers, so a step reads about 1.04 GB of FP8 weights plus the 0.27 GB BF16 tied embedding/lm_head, about 1.30 GB.
impact: At about 0.6 TB/s on 1g.18gb the TPOT floor is about 2.17 ms, which rules out the quoted 91-ERS target without multi-token steps.

article_claim: Optimization level O3 gives a consistent +2%.
finding: Current vLLM documentation says O3 is presently equivalent to O2, the default; behavior is version-dependent.
impact: A +2% from O3 must name the exact vLLM commit and hardware and come from an A/B.

finding: Current vLLM documents fastokens as a Rust backend available in v0.23.0 and later.
impact: Record the Rust package/backend and exact vLLM build; then verify token IDs and streaming output before measuring latency.

article_claim: Reducing --shm-size from 2 GB to 256 MB avoids OOM.
finding: The shm limit is not normally fully preallocated, so the causal link is not shown.
impact: Record cgroup memory.current, /dev/shm usage and the exact failure.
